## EmuTrim 0.6.2

### Highlights

- Added crash-safe `reset AVD_NAME` for EmuTrim-managed AVDs.
- Reset is dry-run by default; `--yes` recreates guest userdata using Android Emulator `-wipe-data`.
- Reset performs a verified cold boot with `-no-snapshot-load`, validates exact emulator identity and boot completion, then stops the exact emulator.
- Added host-side pending-reset recovery state so interrupted resets fail closed and can be safely retried.
- Pending reset blocks ordinary mutable lifecycle operations until recovery completes.
- Reset verifies that stale EmuTrim reversible guest state is absent before completing.

### Reset semantics

`reset` retains the managed AVD definition, SDK, system image, and host `sdcard.img`. It resets guest userdata, installed apps, and settings. `stop`, `reset`, `clear`, and `managed clean` have separate meanings.

### Physical acceptance

Apple Silicon macOS acceptance verified:

- guest userdata was reset
- stale EmuTrim guest state was removed by the wipe
- automatic exact-emulator shutdown succeeded
- a subsequent ordinary start did not restore pre-reset userdata, settings, or EmuTrim slim state
- host `sdcard.img` remained byte-for-byte unchanged

Android Emulator documents that `-wipe-data` does not affect `sdcard.img`. Its simulated SD-card feature is unsupported on Apple Silicon Macs, so guest-visible mounting is not part of macOS acceptance.

### Known limitations

- Windows physical reset acceptance was not performed. Automated Windows CI covers code and path/reparse behavior; physical guest visibility of simulated SD-card contents has not been verified.
- Physical process-interruption recovery was not performed; marker persistence, launch/boot/proof/stop failures, retry, and cleanup are covered by automated tests.
- macOS `stats` remains unsupported.
- Linux remains CI/core-only.
